sections.overview: The brant, called Brent Goose in Europe, is a small Arctic-breeding goose that winters on coasts in Europe, Asia and North America.
sections.identification: It is compact, with dark head and neck, a white neck patch, brownish back and pale undertail; markings vary among populations.
sections.habitat: It nests in Arctic tundra wetlands and winters on sheltered bays, estuaries, lagoons and salt marshes.
sections.diet: In winter it eats mainly eelgrass and other aquatic plants, sometimes shifting to algae or salt-marsh grasses when usual food is scarce.
sections.behavior: It forms sociable flocks outside breeding; routes and wintering grounds differ among dark-bellied, pale-bellied and Pacific populations.
sections.reproduction: Pairs nest on the ground in the Arctic, often in small colonies near water; the female incubates as the male guards.
sections.ecology: It is related to the Canada Goose (Branta canadensis) and Barnacle Goose (B. leucopsis); brants are smaller and especially tied to coastal eelgrass in winter.
sections.conservation: It is globally Least Concern, though regional populations have fluctuated with food supply, habitat change and hunting history.
